thread:
maria: heads up — two prod hosts hit OOM in the last 12h during long interactive sessions. pattern isn't simple allocation spike, looks like gradual KV cache spine fragmentation + page thrash until the slab allocator can't satisfy new kv allocations. hosts: host-42, host-101. both running r2026.03 runtime.

akash: thanks, digging into profiles now. grabbed a heap pprof snap before the second crash — attaching excerpt. looks like a ton of small pinned fragments from prefix reuse + a large number of tiny freelist objects that never coalesce. suspect threshold for coalesce is too high for longctx patterns.

akash: ```
pprof heap 1m-ago
Total: 48 GB
-- kv_slab: 28.9 GB (60%)
   pinned_fragments: 9.2 GB
   freelist_nodes: 6.8 GB
   page_overhead: 12.9 GB
-- runtime_caches: 6.0 GB
-- other: 13.1 GB
Heap growth rate: ~400 MB / 10 min during heavy long-session traffic
```

jon: hmm. any recent kernel selection or batching changes? last rollout swapped to the new multi-kernel path that keeps larger per-shard scratch buffers. could be contributing.

maria: yes we rolled kernel v12 last night (auto batching + dynamic kernel pick). can we confirm kernel change increases peak resident memory?

akash: quick correlation: hosts with v12 showed 15-20% higher resident for same load. v11 hosts stayed under headroom. v12's batch padding combined with aggressive prefetch seems to inflate KV temp allocations.

olivia: immediate mitigations I can push: 1) disable v12 kernel selection for long-session route (will route those requests to v11) 2) lower max_batch_tokens for conversational routes to cut pad blowup 3) enable soft-evict policy on KV cache to aggressively prune stale prefixes once host-resident > headroom*0.85

kevin: also add quick runtime throttle: per-session token cap of 200k (enforce at router) and drop prefix caching for sessions > 50k tokens. That reduces pinned_fragments growth.

rachel: +1 on fallback routing. ops: can we rollout a temporary policy: route any session with predicted context > 100k tokens to dedicated-large (reserved) instances with extra KV headroom?

maria: good idea. but dedicated capacity is limited; we should only route the heaviest sessions after we enable soft-evict. do both: soft-evict everywhere + selective routing to dedicated for >200k.

akash: for a medium-term fix I propose: 1) lower coalesce threshold so freelist nodes merge more aggressively during idle periods 2) add periodic slab compaction job (background, low-priority) that merges contiguous free fragments 3) introduce an L2 spill for very old prefixes (compress and write to async store) and mark them cold so they don't pin memory

jon: implementation note: coalesce lowering interacts with kernel v12 assumptions about stable pointers. need to add a safe quiesce window before compaction to avoid dangling references. that will force a tiny pause for some kernels — measure impact.

maria: ops plan for next 2 hours:
- olivia: rollback kernel v12 selector for conversational route (canary then 100%)
- kevin: patch router to drop prefix caching for sessions >50k and add per-session cap 200k
- akash: flip on KV_SOFT_EVICT and monitor fragmentation signals + emit metric kv.pinned_fragments.bytes
- rachel: notify sales/support about possible degraded long-session behavior and update incident channel

deploy-bot: deploy job queued -> canary to 3 hosts in prod (eng-runtime-canary). CI checks green.

kevin: quick snippet I'll push to router config: ```json
{"session_limits": {"max_tokens": 200000, "disable_prefix_cache_above": 50000}}
```

maria: monitoring checklist — akash add these alerts: kv.pinned_fragments.bytes > 8GB on a single host, slab.coalesce_fail_rate > 0.05, host.rss/headroom > 0.9 -> page to oncall. also create dashboard for fragmentation trend by session length.

akash: added provisional grafana panels and a perf regression test that runs a synthetic long-convo load overnight against v11 vs v12. early run shows v12 failure after ~8 hours while v11 stays stable to 24h.

olivia: rolling the kernel selector back on the canary now. switching heavy traffic routes to v11, will watch headroom.

maria: at 30m: host-42 recovered after soft-evict enabled + rollback. host-101 still shows high page faults, currently isolating traffic.

rachel: follow-ups: assign a small postmortem doc, timeline, and owners. akash -> root cause analysis and perf diff, olivia -> rollout/rollback playbook, kevin -> router/session caps, jon -> kernel selection safety changes. I'll own the incident doc and customer comms.

jon: for longer-term we'd like a smarter placement policy: route long-running sessions to instances with larger slab pools or with spill enabled. also consider having per-session KV compaction triggers (compact rarely-used prefixes per-session).

maria: agreed. let's keep this thread for updates. thanks everyone. :thanks:
